title: Running Your Email AI on Local Models: Ollama, Neuron and Zero Per-Token Bills
author: Juan Rodriguez
excerpt: How to run subject-line generation, segmentation and drafting on models that live on your own server - and when a cloud model is still worth the call.
content:
Every AI feature in your email platform makes an API call, and every API call carries two costs: the per-token bill and the copy of your data that leaves the building. Running the models locally removes both. Here is how that works in practice with Neuron and Ollama, and where the honest limits are.

What actually runs well locally

Most email-marketing AI work is not frontier-model work. Classifying a bounce reason, tagging a subscriber by interest, scoring a subject line, rewriting a paragraph for tone - a 7B to 14B parameter model on a decent GPU handles these without breaking a sweat. The tasks that benefit from bigger models - long-form drafting in a specific voice, nuanced summarization - are the minority of your token spend.

The Neuron side

Neuron's multi-provider design means the model is a configuration choice, not a code change. Point the provider at your local Ollama endpoint and the agents, tools and chat history you already built keep working. The workflow does not change; only where the inference happens does.

The economics

A local model has a flat cost: the server it runs on, which you were already paying for. There is no meter running in the background while an agent rewrites ten thousand subject lines. That changes what you can afford to do - experimentation stops being a budget decision.

Where cloud still wins

Be honest about the ceiling. If a task needs the best available reasoning - a flagship campaign's copy, a tricky segmentation question - route that one call to a frontier cloud model and keep everything else local. A hybrid setup gives you 95% of the privacy and cost win without giving up quality where it is visible.
